correctness.rationale: The full-Farey denominator-bijection with coprime ordered pairs and u+v>N is classical and has the required endpoint normalization. Within [F_k,F_(k+1)) all valid adjacent denominator pairs must involve F_k, because all distinct smaller Fibonacci denominators sum to at most F_k; only F_k+F_(k-1) and F_k+F_(k-2) can exceed the moving threshold at the top. Fibonacci strong divisibility proves both candidate pairs coprime. The resulting final-block length F_(k-3), the initial count E(7)=3, and the Fibonacci recurrence yield E(N)=max(F_(k-2),N-F_k+1) exactly. Quotient monotonicity within every block and Fibonacci limits give the two distinct irrational extremal values. Actual packaged verifier independently cross-checked all full-Farey orders through 450 and all coprime-pair orders through 15000; this finite testing is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The source statements have different domains or adjacency relations: ratios of Fibonacci values (Alladi), consecutive fractions after retaining only a parity class (Boca--Cobeli--Zaharescu and Cobeli--Zaharescu), or a bound by a consecutive-Fibonacci quotient (OEIS A207524). None of the materially inspected assertions provides the exact full-Farey Fibonacci-denominator two-neighbor threshold or the two distinct order-frequency limits. Semantic publication-index queries for equivalent formulations and dominating results found no matching statement. This supports provisional originality but does not guarantee global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The event exactly two full-Farey adjacencies with Fibonacci denominators is a canonical minimal nontrivial sparse-denominator phenomenon; classifying precisely every integer order on which it occurs is a natural complete classification. Its exact block count additionally proves nonexistence of natural density with sharp positive distinct lower and upper density constants. This is not just an arbitrary numerical slice: the Fibonacci recurrence determines a precise arithmetic sawtooth at every scale. No extra claims about all adjacency counts or sparse sets in general are made.
